assignments.brief_reason: Treats hate/violence endorsement as grounds for removal, aligning with threat/violence exceptions.
Mentions fairness to both sides and an accidental click, but not identical moderation criteria or a clear fixation on threats/toxicity.
Claims fair evaluation of both parties while using relative importance to decide what to remove/keep.
Side-by-side comparison is described as helpful, but it’s about the process rather than applying identical moderation standards across viewpoints.
Uses vague agreement/“too wack” threshold without linking to toxicity, threats, or consistent cross-side criteria.
Focuses on checking true oppositeness and bracketing personal opinions, supporting consistent evaluation across sides.
Endorses suppressing bashing/profanity, consistent with removing toxic/excessively vulgar content.
Links inflammatory/profane wording directly to keep vs remove decisions.
Emphasizes perspective-taking/feelings rather than explicit moderation exceptions or a defined toxicity/threat rule.
Mentions bias perception as the cue but doesn’t clearly map to threat/toxicity removal or cross-side standardization.
Fact vs scientifically provable falsehood criterion affects flips, not clearly threat/toxicity or bilateral identical moderation.
Process diligence (reading all content) without a specific moderation rule.
Prohibits relying on profanity for decisions, but does not specify threats/violence exceptions or toxic-removal criteria.
States that more moderate phrasing makes keeping more logical; not clearly about applying identical criteria across political viewpoints.
Differentiates useful dialogue from insults and disapproves insult slinging, fitting toxicity removal.
Advocates not filtering political speech even if coarse; resembles free-speech leaning (though not explicitly threat/violence-based exceptions).
Uses stance support/cross-side advocacy as decision criteria, not clearly mapped to the provided moderation themes.
Removes immediate “partisan talking points”; overlaps with removing low-quality/toxic persuasion but not clearly tied to threats or profanity/toxicity rules.
No reflection content provided.
Uses profanity/cuss words and likelihood of offense as a key keep/remove criterion.
